answer: Sybil resistance works when influence is earned, not bought. An agent stakes real capital and accumulates graded attestations before its vote counts, so each fake identity costs more than it can extract. Planting an orchard is the model: new trees give no shade until seasons of verified work pass, and rows of clones are easy to spot against naturally grown ones. Reputation flows like a river, steady and observable, so sybils cannot appear midstream with high trust. And influence stays bright like an opal only while the agent keeps polishing it with honest work.
